name: identity
title: Identity
summary: Who someone is and how they prove it: accounts for customers, seller members and staff, credentials, email verification, sessions and refresh tokens for the website and the Android app, password recovery, 2-step verification, signed-in devices, guest sessions and the security activity log.
owns: Accounts in two realms: member (customers and seller members share one account) and staff (invite-only: an invitation link plus a pass code; email and password sign-in, no 2-step)
Registration with email verification codes (6 digits, 10 minutes, resend timer)
Phone number verification codes (requested by customers when the mobile number changes)
Sign-in for the store, Seller Center and Admin Center; access tokens plus rotating refresh tokens; keep me signed in
Failed sign-in counting and temporary lockout (attempts left shown to the user)
Password recovery links (single use, 30 minutes) that never reveal whether an account exists; password change; forced reset by staff
Optional 2-step verification for members (authenticator app at launch, text message later), recovery codes, trusted devices
Signed-in devices with sign-out of one device or everywhere
Seller context: which seller accounts a member may act for, and switching between them
Invitations for staff and seller members (accept link, password set-up; staff also enter the invitation pass code)
Guest sessions (X-Guest-Session) for cart, recently viewed and guest checkout; guest order access grants on a guest session; emailed order links
Security activity log per account (sign-ins, failures, password and 2-step changes, staff actions on the account)
Staff tools to lock, unlock, force a password reset, reset 2-step, sign out and disable accounts
Recent re-authentication (re-auth tokens) before sensitive actions such as account closure or payout destination changes
notOwns: Customer profile, phone number on the profile, addresses, marketing consent and account closure rules (open orders, returns, cases): customers. identity closes the credential when customers calls closeAccount
Guest order lookup form (order reference + checkout email) and 'email me my order links': customers. It verifies the order with orders, then calls grantGuestOrderAccess / issueOrderLink here
Seller members, seller roles and seller permissions (who may change payouts, etc.): sellers. identity only stores which sellers an account may act for (grantSellerContext)
Staff roles, permissions, approval limits and the combined 'invite staff with roles' action: access (it calls inviteStaff here)
Sending emails and texts (codes, reset links, security alerts): notifications, which consumes identity events
Notification channel preferences: notifications; promotional (marketing) consent: customers
Material staff action history: audit (identity also keeps its own security activity log per account)

publicApi.name: getAccount
publicApi.signature: (accountId: uuid) => AccountSummary | null
publicApi.desc: Email, display name, status, 2-step state

publicApi.name: getAccounts
publicApi.signature: (accountIds: uuid[]) => AccountSummary[]
publicApi.desc: Batch lookup for lists (staff directory, seller members, audit names)

publicApi.name: findAccountByEmail
publicApi.signature: (email: string, realm: 'member' | 'staff') => AccountSummary | null
publicApi.desc: Used when inviting someone who may already have an account

publicApi.name: inviteStaff
publicApi.signature: (input: { email: string, name: string, invitedBy: Actor }) => StaffInvitationIssued
publicApi.desc: Create an invited staff account and send the accept link (event identity.invitation.created). Returns the invitation with its link and pass code in-process (the pass code is never in the event, an HTTP response or a log; the server tools print it). access assigns the roles.

publicApi.name: inviteSellerMember
publicApi.signature: (input: { email: string, name: string, sellerId: uuid, sellerName: string, invitedBy: Actor }) => Invitation
publicApi.desc: Invite a person to act for a seller. Reuses an existing member account when the email has one.

publicApi.name: revokeInvitation
publicApi.signature: (invitationId: uuid, input: { reason: string, by: Actor, contextRef?: string }) => Invitation
publicApi.desc: Cancel a pending invitation (the accept link stops working at once) and publish identity.invitation.revoked. contextRef, when given, must match the invitation's (sellers passes its sellerId so a seller can only revoke its own member invitations; NOT_FOUND otherwise). Revoking an invitation that is already revoked returns it unchanged; an accepted or expired one fails with ILLEGAL_TRANSITION.

publicApi.name: grantSellerContext
publicApi.signature: (input: { accountId: uuid, sellerId: uuid, memberId: uuid, sellerName: string, roleLabel: string, isOwner: bool }) => void
publicApi.desc: Allow a member account to sign in to Seller Center for this seller (NOT_FOUND for other accounts). Idempotent: called again to refresh the seller name, role label or owner flag, and to grant access again after revokeSellerContext (a reactivated member). A different memberId (a re-invited member) ends the sessions bound to the old membership. Only sellers writes these grants.

publicApi.name: revokeSellerContext
publicApi.signature: (accountId: uuid, sellerId: uuid, reason: string) => void
publicApi.desc: Remove seller access and revoke sessions bound to that seller

publicApi.name: revokeSessions
publicApi.signature: (accountId: uuid, reason: string, audience?: 'store' | 'seller' | 'admin') => int
publicApi.desc: Sign an account out everywhere (or in one area). Returns the number of sessions revoked.

publicApi.name: grantGuestOrderAccess
publicApi.signature: (guestSessionId: uuid, orderId: uuid, email: string, via: 'checkout' | 'lookup' | 'link') => GuestSession
publicApi.desc: Let a guest session open one order (after guest checkout, a successful lookup in customers, or an emailed link)

publicApi.name: hasGuestOrderAccess
publicApi.signature: (guestSessionId: uuid, orderId: uuid) => bool
publicApi.desc: Gate guest access to order detail, tracking, returns and help

publicApi.name: issueOrderLink
publicApi.signature: (orderId: uuid, email: string) => { url: url, expiresAt: datetime }
publicApi.desc: Signed link for confirmation and 'email me my order links' emails; redeemed at POST /api/public/identity/order-links/{token}/redeem

publicApi.name: closeAccount
publicApi.signature: (accountId: uuid, reason: string) => void
publicApi.desc: Close the member credential after customers completes a closure. Revokes all sessions; keeps Seller Center access if the account still belongs to a seller.

publicApi.name: sendPasswordReset
publicApi.signature: (accountId: uuid, input: { reason: string, by: Actor, revokeSessions: bool }) => void
publicApi.desc: Staff-initiated reset from another module's screen (customers account actions)

publicApi.name: startPhoneVerification
publicApi.signature: (accountId: uuid, phone: string) => VerificationChallenge
publicApi.desc: Text a 6-digit code to a new mobile number (needs SMS, phase 2; until then the number stays unverified). Confirmed at POST /api/public/identity/verifications/{id}/confirm; publishes identity.user.verified with channel phone.

publicApi.name: verifyReauthToken
publicApi.signature: (principal: Principal, token: string, purpose: string) => bool
publicApi.desc: True only when the re-auth token was issued for this purpose (the endpoint's step-up purpose) to this account, session, audience and seller, and is unused and unexpired. A token issued for another purpose is refused. Does not consume it. access and returns check approvals above stepUpAbove with it (purpose approval).

publicApi.name: accountSecurityOf
publicApi.signature: (accountIds: uuid[], opts?: { activityLimit?: int }) => Map<uuid, AccountSecurity>
publicApi.desc: Batched staff view of sign-in security for customer 360 views: AccountAdmin (lock, forced reset, 2-step, devices, recent security activity) plus email status, warnings and a one-line sign-in summary. Callers pass identity account ids (Customer.userId).

publicApi.name: consumeReauthToken
publicApi.signature: (token: string) => bool
publicApi.desc: Claims a verified re-auth token for one request: marks it used only if it is still unused, and returns true when this call marked it (a second request with the same token gets false and is refused). Called by the kernel after verifying the token, before the handler runs, and by access and returns for approvals above stepUpAbove.

publicApi.name: releaseReauthToken
publicApi.signature: (token: string) => void
publicApi.desc: Puts back a re-auth token claimed by a request that then failed, so the person can retry without confirming again; called by the kernel, access and returns.

publicApi.name: revocationsSince
publicApi.signature: (cursor?: string) => { sessions: { sessionId: uuid, at: datetime }[], accounts: { accountId: uuid, validAfter: datetime }[], cursor: string }
publicApi.desc: Revoked sessions and account-wide revocations (tokens issued before validAfter) since a cursor; every server polls this every few seconds and loads the last access-token lifetime on startup.

publicApi.name: verifyRefreshToken
publicApi.signature: (refreshToken: string) => { sessionId: uuid, accountId?: uuid, audience: string, kind: string } | null
publicApi.desc: Middleware check for refresh and sign-out: the session the refresh token belongs to (also during the reuse grace window), or null when it is unknown, expired, revoked or reused.

publicApi.name: touchStaffSession
publicApi.signature: (sessionId: uuid) => { live: bool, reason?: 'revoked' | 'expired' | 'idle' | 'unknown' }
publicApi.desc: Middleware check on every admin request (each server caches the answer 5 s per session): whether the staff session is still live (not revoked, not past its expiry or absolute limit, and active within staffIdleMinutes), recording the activity (sessions.last_active_at, at most once a minute) that keeps it from going idle.

stateMachines.name: Account status
stateMachines.notes: Staff accounts start as invited (initial state for that realm); member accounts start pending_verification and cannot sign in until the email code is confirmed (sign-in returns EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED with a fresh challenge). Automatic locks (failed sign-ins) expire after lockoutMinutes; staff locks have an optional end date. Every move writes a security_events row; staff-initiated moves are also audited. Unverified accounts older than 7 days are deleted by identity.purge-expired.

stateMachines.name: Session
stateMachines.notes: refresh rotates the refresh token; presenting the previous token again (reuse) revokes the session and records refresh_token_reused. passwordChanged revokes other sessions only when signOutOtherDevices is chosen (always for forced resets). Staff sessions have an absolute limit of 12 hours.

stateMachines.name: Verification challenge
stateMachines.notes: Codes are 6 digits, stored hashed, valid 10 minutes, 5 attempts. Resend issues a new code on the same challenge after resendAvailableAt (60 s). A new email change supersedes the previous one.

stateMachines.name: Invitation
stateMachines.notes: Links are valid 7 days. Resend issues a new token (and, for staff, a new pass code) and invalidates the old one. The 5th wrong pass code revokes a staff invitation but keeps its account invited and its roles waiting, so a resend (npm run staff-link) can give a new link; a revoked invitation whose account was closed (a cancelled invitation) cannot be resent.

endpoints.summary: Create a customer account and send an email code
endpoints.desc: Always answers 202 with a challenge so the form cannot be used to discover accounts: if the email already has an account, the email says so and offers sign-in and password reset, and the code will not verify. Password rules are checked live with GET /password-policy and again here.

endpoints.summary: Confirm an email or phone code (registration, email change, phone change)
endpoints.desc: Registration: activates the account and signs the customer in; guest orders placed with this email can then be attached (identity.user.verified, consumed by customers). Email change: switches the sign-in email and alerts the old address. Phone: marks the number verified (identity.user.verified with channel phone).

endpoints.summary: Send a new code
Sign in with email and password
endpoints.desc: Returns tokens, or a 2-step challenge, or (seller audience with several sellers) the list of sellers to choose from. Wrong passwords return INVALID_CREDENTIALS with details.attemptsLeft; at the limit the account locks for lockoutMinutes and ACCOUNT_LOCKED carries details.lockedUntil. Unknown emails get the same answer and timing. A guest session passed in is claimed (cart and recently viewed merge). A sign-in from a device not seen before publishes identity.session.new_device for the security alert.

endpoints.summary: Complete sign-in with a 2-step code or recovery code
Text the 2-step code to the saved phone
Exchange a refresh token for new tokens
endpoints.desc: Rotates the refresh token. Presenting an already-rotated token revokes the session (theft signal) and returns REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID. The Android app calls this when an access token expires.

audience.desc: Website: the app calling, whose refresh cookie (__Secure-mk_refresh_<audience>) is used. Each app has its own cookie, so signing into one app doesn't replace another's session in the same browser. Android leaves it out

refreshToken.desc: Android; the website sends its app's refresh cookie and audience instead

endpoints.summary: Sign out this device
endpoints.desc: Works for every audience; the refresh token identifies the session. Idempotent.

audience.desc: Website: the app calling, whose refresh cookie (__Secure-mk_refresh_<audience>) is used. Each app has its own cookie, so signing into one app doesn't replace another's session in the same browser. Android leaves it out

refreshToken.desc: Android; the website sends its app's refresh cookie and audience instead

endpoints.summary: Email a password reset link
endpoints.desc: Always 202 with the masked email, whether or not an account exists. The link works once and expires in 30 minutes; a new request invalidates the previous link.

endpoints.summary: Check a reset link before showing the new-password form
Set a new password from a reset link
endpoints.desc: Clears lockouts. Signs out other devices when chosen (always for forced resets). The account owner gets a confirmation email.

endpoints.summary: Password rules for the live checklist
Start an app session: the visitor token every request needs
endpoints.desc: The only endpoint without a token. Requires an app proof in X-App-Proof (Play Integrity on Android, bot challenge on the website). Returns a visitor access token and refresh token for the app named in audience. In the store the visitor session is also the guest session (cart, recently viewed, guest checkout, guest order grants). Signing in or registering with the visitor token claims the session into the account.

endpoints.summary: Open an order from an emailed link
endpoints.desc: Grants the (new or given) guest session access to that order. Signed-in customers whose verified email matches see it in their account instead.

endpoints.summary: Show an invitation (staff or seller member)
Accept an invitation and set a password
endpoints.desc: Seller members: signs in to Seller Center for the inviting seller. Staff: passCode is required (the pass code handed over with the link); the account becomes active and is signed in to the Admin Center at once. A wrong pass code is PASS_CODE_INVALID with details.attemptsLeft; the 5th revokes the link (npm run staff-link gives a new link and pass code).

endpoints.summary: Continue with Google or Apple
endpoints.desc: Members only. Links to an existing account only when the provider confirms the same verified email.

endpoints.summary: Sign-in and security page in one call
endpoints.desc: Also used by seller members from Seller Center (same member account; the store-area security endpoints accept a member session of either audience).

endpoints.summary: Change password
Change sign-in email (sends a code to the new address)
endpoints.desc: Confirmed with POST /api/public/identity/verifications/{id}/confirm. The old address stays active until then.

endpoints.summary: Confirm it's you before a sensitive action
endpoints.desc: Returns a single-use re-auth token valid reauthTokenMinutes for the requested purpose, bound to the account and session: account-closure (customers), email-change, two-step-removal and recovery-codes. Seller Center uses POST /api/seller/identity/reauth for payout-account, business-change and seller-closure.

endpoints.summary: Confirm it is you before a sensitive Seller Center action
endpoints.desc: Same check as the store re-auth (password or 2-step code) on the seller session. Returns a single-use re-auth token valid reauthTokenMinutes, bound to the account, the purpose and the current seller context (if one is chosen); purposes payout-account, business-change and seller-closure (sellers). A token taken before a seller is chosen does not work once one is.

endpoints.summary: Confirm it is you before a sensitive Admin Center action
endpoints.desc: The staff member re-enters their password (staff have no 2-step). Returns a single-use re-auth token valid reauthTokenMinutes, bound to the account, session and purpose: role-grant (access roles and invitations), staff-account (staff accounts and invitations), payout-destination (finance payout destinations) and approval (approving a request above access stepUpAbove).

endpoints.summary: Start turning on 2-step verification
endpoints.desc: Members only: staff accounts sign in with email and password and cannot add a 2-step method (TWO_STEP_NOT_FOR_STAFF).

endpoints.summary: Confirm the first code; returns recovery codes once
endpoints.desc: Members only (TWO_STEP_NOT_FOR_STAFF for staff accounts).

endpoints.summary: Turn off a 2-step method
Replace recovery codes
Where you're signed in
endpoints.desc: Small and bounded (maxDevicesPerAccount), so not paged.

Sign out everywhere
Recent security activity
Sellers this member can act for (seller switcher)

endpoints.desc: Re-issues tokens bound to the chosen seller. Every later seller-area request acts only for that seller.

endpoints.desc: Staff realm results need identity.staff-accounts.manage as well. Roles of staff come from GET /api/admin/access/members.

Lock an account (suspected compromise, offboarding)

endpoints.desc: Member accounts (staff accounts have no 2-step). The member can turn 2-step on again from their security page. The identity check performed is recorded.

identityCheck.desc: How the person was verified (video call, ID document…)

endpoints.summary: Sign an account out everywhere
Disable a staff account (offboarding)
endpoints.desc: Revokes sessions. access consumes identity.account.disabled to end role assignments and flag lead/backup gaps.

endpoints.summary: Re-enable a disabled staff account
endpoints.desc: Roles are not restored automatically; assign them again in access.

endpoints.summary: Security activity of one account
Staff invitations
Resend a staff invitation (new 7-day link)
endpoints.desc: Issues a new link and pass code (the old ones stop working). The pass code is not shown here: the server operator prints the link and pass code with npm run staff-link and hands them over.

INVALID_CREDENTIALS.meaning: Email and password don't match. details.attemptsLeft before a temporary lock.

ACCOUNT_LOCKED.meaning: Sign-in is paused. details.lockedUntil (null = until staff unlock) and details.cause.

ACCOUNT_DISABLED.meaning: The account is disabled or closed.

EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED.meaning: Confirm the email first. details.challenge is a fresh VerificationChallenge.

CODE_EXPIRED.meaning: The code or challenge has expired; request a new one.

CHALLENGE_LOCKED.meaning: Too many wrong codes; start again.

WEAK_PASSWORD.meaning: The password breaks a rule. details.failed lists the rules (min_length, number, uppercase, personal_info, breached).

PASSWORD_REUSED.meaning: The password was used recently on this account.

PASSWORD_NOT_SET.meaning: The account has no password (it signs in with Google or Apple), so it cannot confirm with one. Not counted as a failed attempt; confirm with a 2-step code where the endpoint accepts one.

RESET_LINK_INVALID.meaning: The reset link was used, replaced or has expired.

REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID.meaning: Refresh token unknown, expired, revoked or reused; sign in again.

EMAIL_IN_USE.meaning: Another account in this realm uses that email.

METHOD_NOT_AVAILABLE.meaning: That 2-step method is not enabled yet (SMS is phase 2).

TWO_STEP_NOT_FOR_STAFF.meaning: Staff accounts sign in with email and password only; they cannot add a 2-step method.

INVITATION_INVALID.meaning: The invitation was accepted, revoked or has expired.

PASS_CODE_INVALID.meaning: The invitation pass code is missing or wrong. details.attemptsLeft; the 5th wrong pass code revokes the link (ask the server operator for a new link and pass code).

SELF_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED.meaning: Staff cannot lock, disable or reset their own account.

ORDER_LINK_INVALID.meaning: The order link has expired; use Guest order lookup.

APP_PROOF_INVALID.meaning: The app proof (Play Integrity or bot challenge) is missing or failed.

notes: Realms: a member account serves both the store and Seller Center; seller access comes from seller_access rows that only the sellers module writes. Staff accounts are separate and invite-only; the same email may exist once in each realm.

Staff sign-in without an authenticator (owner decision 2026-10-14: the server runs offline and only staff use it). A staff invitation comes with a pass code (8 characters, XXXX-XXXX, no 0/O/1/I/L) that the server operator prints with npm run bootstrap-owner or npm run staff-link and hands over with the link; only its hash is stored, and it is never in identity.invitation.created, an HTTP response or a log. Accepting takes the link token, the pass code and a new password and signs the person in. Staff then sign in with email and password, have no 2-step methods (they cannot add one), and confirm sensitive actions by re-entering the password (POST /api/admin/identity/reauth → reauthToken). Members keep their optional 2-step unchanged.

Audience is chosen at sign-in (store | seller | admin). A token for one audience is rejected by the other API areas with UNAUTHORIZED, except that the store-area security endpoints (/security, /password, /two-step/*, /devices, /security-activity) accept any member session, so seller staff manage their own sign-in security with the same endpoints.

Seller context: a seller-audience session acts for exactly one seller at a time. With one seller the context is set at sign-in; with several, sign-in returns seller_context_required and the app calls POST /api/seller/identity/session/seller-context. Seller-area paths never contain a seller id; the token carries it.
Account discovery is prevented: registration, password reset and sign-in respond the same way (and with similar timing) whether or not the email exists.

Events marked SENSITIVE (codes, reset and invitation links) are delivered in-process to notifications only. When the outbox is introduced these events are excluded from it and from logs; notifications must not store the code or link in the delivery log (it stores the template version and a redacted body).

Guest flow: a guest session (X-Guest-Session) is created on the first add to cart and carries the cart, recently viewed and guest checkout. After guest checkout, checkout calls grantGuestOrderAccess (via checkout) and issueOrderLink (link in the confirmation email). The lookup form and 'email me my order links' are served by customers, which verifies the order with orders and then calls grantGuestOrderAccess (via lookup) or issueOrderLink. orders, shipping, returns and support check hasGuestOrderAccess. When a customer verifies an email (identity.user.verified) or signs in with a guest session (identity.guest_session.claimed), customers, orders, cart and search attach the guest data by consuming the event; identity calls none of them in-process.
Staff 'invite with roles' is one action in access (POST /api/admin/access/staff-invitations) which calls inviteStaff here; identity's admin endpoints cover resend, revoke and account security only.

Every security-relevant change writes a security_events row (shown to the account owner). Staff actions on accounts are also recorded in audit via audit.record (optional dependency: if audit is disabled they are still in security_events).
Rate limits: sign-in 10/min per IP and 5/15 min per email; registration and password reset 5/hour per email and 20/hour per IP; guest sessions 30/hour per IP.

Business values (lockout length, password rules, token lifetimes) are defaults to confirm; screen copy differs (register says 10 characters, the security page says 12): proposal is 10 for members and 12 for staff.

Every request carries a token (auth design v3, docs/03-auth-middleware.md). Visitor tokens come from POST /api/public/identity/app-sessions (bootstrap, app proof) and have the same JWT format as access tokens with kind visitor. The store visitor session is the guest session (guest_sessions table); X-Guest-Session is retired. Sign-in and registration called with a visitor token claim that session.

Access and visitor tokens are EdDSA JWTs: typ at+jwt, iss marketly-identity, aud store|seller|admin, kind, sub, sid, sellerId, memberId, authAt, twoStepAt, name (the display name recorded with what the person does, at most 80 characters; a name change shows after the next refresh), iat, exp, jti; public keys published by kid (AUTH_JWKS). Re-auth, reset, invitation and order-link tokens are opaque and travel in request bodies, never in URL paths.
